chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who entrusts the matter of his wife to a man, and he said: 'Bear witness that I have entrusted the matter of so-and-so to so-and-so,' and he divorces her, is that permissible? He said: 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Is a divorce valid if a husband delegates the authority to his wife's affairs to an agent?
ai.summary: This hadith from *al-Istibsar* establishes the permissibility of *wakala* (agency) in divorce, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence allowing a husband to delegate the pronouncement of talaq to a representative. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the validity of this arrangement, emphasizing that the agent's action is legally binding as if performed by the husband himself, provided the delegation is clear. This ruling underscores the flexibility of marital contracts in Shia law, facilitating divorce procedures when the husband is absent or unable to act directly.
